At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Who We Are

For 150 years, London Health Sciences Centre (LHSC) has been a leader in world-class care. As an acute tertiary and quaternary teaching hospital, LHSC provides leading-edge medical care to people from across western Ontario and beyond. LHSC is located just two hours from Toronto and two hours from Detroit in the city of London which is known for its beautiful and walkable downtown core located on the Thames River, a vibrant culinary scene and scores of activities that highlight local arts, culture and music. Our team of more than 17,000 physicians, staff, learners and volunteers works tirelessly to support patients as they navigate their unique health-care journeys. As one of Canada’s largest acute-care teaching hospitals, LHSC is a renowned centre of innovation with a history of groundbreaking research that has influenced how people are cared for around the world. With nearly 1 million annual patient visits across University, Victoria and Children's Hospitals, LHSC provides compassionate leading-edge care and is proud of our strong regional, national and international partnerships. For more information, please visit www.lhsc.on.ca.

The Business Support team provides portfolios with operational budgeting, reporting, forecasting and analysis support. This team plays an important role in assisting LHSC leadership in making informed financial decisions, and provides sound advice in financial practices and organizational policy.

The Capital Finance team supports the capital asset needs of LHSC. The team works closely with Corporate Accounting to ensure accurate, efficient and timely recording of capital transactions. The culture of teamwork and respect drives the team to support the capital needs of patient care at LHSC.

What the Role is

The Director, Business Support and Capital Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for business management and capital planning practices across London Health Sciences Centre (LHSC) to maximize delivery of high quality, safe, and efficient patient care within available budgets. The role provides hospital-wide leadership and oversight for business planning, financial management, reporting, and control practices to safeguard organizational assets and strengthen financial performance. The Director also provides strategic financial stewardship of LHSC's capital planning, capital accounting, and capital funding activities and ensures compliance with internal and external audit requirements related to capital financial reporting.

The Director leads and drives systems transformation through encouraging and supporting innovation and championing and orchestrating change, challenging the status quo. The Director develops purposeful coalitions with internal and external stakeholders.

Apply defined guardrails and scenario analysis to assess profitability, capacity, factory utilization, service requirements, risk, and incremental growth.

The Executive Vice President of Regional Management is responsible for overseeing the company's regional business operations, developing regional management strategies, and ensuring effective execution of corporate objectives across assigned geographic markets.

This executive provides strategic direction to regional leadership teams, monitors regional business performance, manages operational priorities, and identifies opportunities for business expansion and organizational development.

The role works closely with the CEO, COO, and other senior executives to align regional activities with corporate strategies, strengthen management accountability, improve operational performance, and support the company's long-term growth.

1. Regional Strategy and Executive Leadership

Develop and implement regional management strategies aligned with the company's overall corporate objectives.

Establish regional business priorities, management objectives, and long-term development plans.

Translate corporate strategies into actionable regional execution plans.

Provide strategic direction and executive oversight to regional directors, managers, and business unit leaders.

Evaluate regional market conditions and identify opportunities for business growth and operational improvement.

Advise the CEO and senior leadership team on regional business performance, expansion opportunities, and management priorities.

Ensure regional teams operate in accordance with corporate policies, operational standards, and established business objectives.

Evaluate revenue performance, operating expenses, productivity, and regional business growth.

Hold regional executives and department leaders accountable for performance outcomes.

Identify performance gaps and direct the development of corrective action plans.

Present regular regional performance assessments and strategic recommendations to executive leadership.

Identify new geographic markets and business opportunities for regional expansion.

Evaluate market conditions, competitive environments, and regional business potential.

Develop regional growth strategies in collaboration with business development and corporate strategy teams.

Oversee the execution of regional expansion initiatives and new market development programs.

Build relationships with regional business partners, industry stakeholders, and strategic organizations.

Assess the operational and financial requirements associated with regional expansion.

5. Senior Management and Organizational Development

Recruit, lead, mentor, and develop regional senior management personnel in coordination with the appropriate departments.

Establish leadership expectations, management responsibilities, and organizational accountability.

Evaluate regional leadership effectiveness and identify succession planning needs.

Strengthen communication and coordination between corporate headquarters and regional management teams.

Develop management structures that support regional growth and organizational scalability.

Promote a results-oriented leadership culture across all assigned regions.

Oversee regional budget planning and resource allocation in coordination with the finance department.

Review regional operating budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure performance.

Ensure regional resources are aligned with corporate priorities and business requirements.

Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency and operational productivity.

Evaluate the financial implications of regional business initiatives and expansion plans.

Work with finance leadership to maintain appropriate financial oversight and budget accountability.

Collaborate with the COO, CFO, regional directors, and other senior executives to coordinate corporate and regional priorities.

Ensure effective cooperation between regional operations, finance, marketing, sales, customer experience, and business development teams.

Resolve major cross-regional management challenges and organizational issues.

Facilitate communication between corporate headquarters and regional business units.

Coordinate strategic initiatives that require participation from multiple departments or geographic markets.

Ensure regional execution remains consistent with company-wide business strategies.

Oversee regional management practices to ensure alignment with corporate governance requirements.

Identify regional operational, financial, and business risks and coordinate appropriate mitigation strategies.

Ensure regional management teams follow established company policies and internal control procedures.

Work with legal, compliance, and internal audit teams on regional governance matters.

Escalate significant regional business risks and management issues to executive leadership.

Promote transparency, accountability, and responsible decision-making across regional operations.

Provide regular reports on regional business performance, operational results, and strategic initiatives.

Present regional management updates and recommendations to the CEO and executive leadership team.

Evaluate the effectiveness of regional strategies and recommend adjustments when necessary.

Provide executive-level insights into market developments, organizational performance, and expansion opportunities.
